crsp_permno.what: CRSP's PERMNO: a permanent number per security that never changes on a name change, ticker change, relisting or delisting; tickers are reused, so a ticker never identifies a security on its own.

openfigi.what: FIGI (venue) < composite FIGI (country) < share-class FIGI (global). 'FIGIs never change, are never reused, and are permanent' across corporate actions; tickers 'can change … which often results in the need to remap content'.

massive_ticker_events.what: Massive's ticker details carry composite_figi and share_class_figi; /vX/reference/tickers/{id}/events?types=ticker_change lists when a company took a ticker (what scripts/history-cut.mjs already reads).

lean_map_files.what: LEAN map files: a CSV per security 'ordered as {date, mapped symbol}'; FirstDate is the listing, 'the last date in the map file is indicative of a delisting event'; GetMappedSymbol(date) resolves which ticker the security had on a date. Factor files: date, price factor, split factor per corporate action.

zipline_assets.what: zipline-reloaded's asset database records 'asset lifetimes and the symbol to asset id (sid) mapping'; 'symbols may map to different firms or underlying assets at different times', so symbol() resolves 'the equity that held the ticker symbol on the current symbol lookup date'; adjustments (splits, mergers, dividends) are a separate writer applied at read time.

nautilus_timestamps.what: NautilusTrader keeps two clocks on every bar: ts_event ('when the event occurred') and ts_init ('when NautilusTrader initialized the object'); time bars default to ts_event = bar close with LEFT_OPEN intervals.

massive_finality.what: Massive: per-day bars are 'continuously recalculated through the session, so it absorbs even very late trades'; bars are 'revised for about 15 minutes on the stream and again at the end of the day'; since 16 Sep 2025 'aggregates that should have included the official close price' land '15 minutes after market close' (they 'were delayed until midnight' before). Cancellation/correction marks 'appear days after the session'; 'for settled history, check again a few days after the session'. Whole market in one call: /v2/aggs/grouped/locale/us/market/stocks/{date}; adjusted=true 'change[s] retroactively when a ticker splits' — store unadjusted for a permanent record.

massive_splits.what: Splits endpoint: execution_date ('the adjustment is applied overnight'), split_from/split_to, historical_adjustment_factor: 'for a price on date D, find the first split whose execution_date is after date D and multiply the unadjusted price by the historical_adjustment_factor'.

exchange_calendars.what: exchange_calendars (XNYS): is_session, previous_session, session_close, early closes flagged per session (the day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve); 'an exchange [is] open only during periods of regular trading'.

arcticdb.what: ArcticDB: 'write, append and update increment the version number'; append 'only accepts data for which the index of the first row is equal to or greater than the index of the last row in the existing data'; update replaces a date range in its entirety; by default older versions are NOT removed (prune_previous_versions opt-in); snapshots pin a state; read as_of a version or a datetime; delete_data_in_range creates a new version.

dbt_tests.what: dbt: not_null, unique, accepted_values, relationships by name per column; dbt-utils: accepted_range, sequential_values, recency ('a timestamp column contains data at least as recent as a defined date interval'), expression_is_true, equal_rowcount; each test fails by NAME with a severity.

great_expectations.what: Great Expectations: expectations named per check (expect_column_values_to_be_between, …_to_be_increasing, …_to_not_be_null, expect_table_row_count_to_be_between, expect_column_pair_values_A_to_be_greater_than_B) with a validation result per expectation.

one_security_many_tickers.finding: Every public store keys history on a PERMANENT id (PERMNO, sid, FIGI) and keeps the ticker-to-id mapping as DATED ROWS. We key on the ticker string and bolt two side tables onto it (floors, joins) that only work if every image carries them. The 29 Sep regrow and the 30 Sep deadlock are both consequences of the id living in images instead of in the data.
one_security_many_tickers.answer_to_alan: Yes, the store should key on a permanent id. The cheapest permanent id we already have is Massive's share_class_figi (scripts/history-cut.mjs reads it today). Plan: (1) every stored object carries identity { share_class_figi, ticker_segments:[{ticker, from_et, through_et}] } written by the one writer; (2) floors and joins become rows of that identity, derived from Massive's ticker events, with the reviewed overrides kept; (3) R2 keys stay by ticker for now (the readers address tickers), but a writer refuses to touch an object whose stored FIGI differs from the request's — the identity check (BF6) then catches a reused string without any floor file. This is LEAN's map file / zipline's sid, done inside the object.

when_a_bar_is_final.finding: Massive says the daily bar is recalculated through the session and revised about 15 minutes after the close and again at end of day; the official close lands ~16:15 ET since Sep 2025 (before that, midnight — which is the 'why so late' Alan asked about: the midnight wait was Massive's old behaviour, and our 04:00 deadline and P10's own-close-first were built around it). Corrections can land DAYS later, so 'final' is a label with a date, never a flag.
when_a_bar_is_final.answer_to_alan: Our FIN1 (values captured after the close) matches Nautilus's two-clock idea and Massive's advice. What we lack is the 'check again a few days later' part: a settled close is confirmed once and never re-read. The night watchman re-reads yesterday AND the four sessions before it (REPLACE verdict on 'confirm once').

adjustments.finding: LEAN and zipline store UNADJUSTED prices plus factor files and adjust at read time; Massive's own advice is the same ('store unadjusted … your history will quietly change under you'). We store ADJUSTED bars, so a split rewrites 23 years of history and the tail merge correctly refuses the overlap and sends the cell to a full rebuild — right, expensive, and invisible.
adjustments.answer_to_alan: Not changed today (every reader expects adjusted). Plan: pull adjusted=false into a sibling namespace for D only, keep the split ledger we already have (AD1), and let the night watchman name every name whose adjusted history changed shape (a split happened) so a rebuild is expected, not a mystery.

history_storage_and_replacement.finding: ArcticDB never shortens in place: append must start after the last row, update replaces a stated range, every write is a new VERSION and the old one stays unless pruned, snapshots pin states. Our 'never shorter' is a GUARD ON A REWRITE; theirs is a property of the storage.
history_storage_and_replacement.answer_to_alan: Replace the guard with versions: write the new object to a versioned key (…/<name>.json.gz is the pointer, …/_v/<name>/<acquired_utc>.json.gz the version), keep the last 3 versions, and let a writer SHORTEN on purpose when it says why (history_cut) — the cut becomes a version with a reason, not a fight with a guard. Until that lands, the P11 cut-before-compare stays (KEEP) and the object's requested_from is corrected by the cut (CHANGE, done).

data_quality_tests.finding: dbt/Great Expectations run named checks on a schedule and fail by name with a severity; Soda adds freshness. We have the checks scattered inside writers (assertStrictSeries, validBar, finality) and no nightly run that reads what we SERVE against an outside source.
data_quality_tests.answer_to_alan: Built: the night watchman (services/stocks-ops/nightly-verdict.mjs) — Massive's whole-market file and FMP's end-of-day vs our daily close and the board's previous close for all 590 names, every Geiger cell, every rung's freshness, every floor — one JSON per night with named causes and one alarm. First run on 2 Oct's session: 590/590 closes exactly equal to Massive's file.
